hero.kicker: Shrub and hedge trimming in Davison, MI
hero.title: Each shrub cut **at the right time.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes trims Davison shrubs and hedges back to clean lines, rakes the clippings out of the beds and hauls them off. Overgrown bushes past saving can come out, roots and all, and Rob will tell you which is which.

local.title: Davison shrubs, sorted **by bloom time.**
local.intro: Most Davison yards have a row of foundation shrubs and a few flowering ones, and the age of the planting shows. Some just need shaping. Others have grown over a window or crowded the front walk. When each one blooms decides when it should be cut.

points.title: Spring bloomers after bloom
points.body: MSU Extension says spring-flowering shrubs like lilac, forsythia, spirea and weigela are best pruned right after they finish blooming, because they set next year's buds the summer before. Cut them in early spring and the flowers go with the clippings.

points.title: Off the walk and the windows
points.body: On compact city lots, a shrub by the front walk can crowd the sidewalk the city expects you to keep clear in winter. We cut it back off the concrete and away from the siding.

points.title: Long hedges on township lots
points.body: Township lots often have a hedge or a shrub row along a drive or a property line. We keep the faces straight and the tops level, then rake the clippings out of the bed underneath.

points.title: When to start over
points.body: Shrubs that are bare inside or far too big for the spot may never recover from a hard cut. A track loader can take them out, roots and all, and the bed can be [rebuilt](/landscaping-davison-mi/).

logistics.title: A shrub trimming visit in Davison.
body: Rob walks the beds with you, notes which shrubs flower in spring and which do not, and plans the visits around that. On the day, we shape each shrub, clean the cuttings out from underneath, blow off the walks and haul the brush away in our trailer.
Davison Township allows brush burning with a permit, and the yard waste truck takes tied bundles. Our clippings leave in our trailer instead, so you skip both.

faq.q: Do you trim shrubs and hedges in Davison, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes trims shrubs and hedges in the City of Davison and Davison Township, from foundation shrubs to long hedges along a drive. We rake out the clippings and haul them away, and the estimate is free.

faq.q: When should I trim my lilacs?
faq.a: Right after they bloom. MSU Extension explains that lilacs and other spring-flowering shrubs form next year's flower buds the summer before, so cutting them in early spring removes the flowers. Dead or damaged wood can come out whenever you find it.

faq.q: Can you remove old bushes in Davison?
faq.a: Yes. Overgrown bushes and small trees come out with a compact track loader, roots and all. One of our Google reviews describes Rob's crew removing 25 year old bushes and a cherry tree, then redoing the bed. Big trees are not something we take down.

They go in our trailer and leave with us. In Davison Township, yard waste bundles have to be tied, under 4 feet long and under 50 pounds, with branches no thicker than 2 inches. Hauling them off saves you the bundling.
